steps.body: Keep climbing down. Split one tenth into 10 equal parts and each is a **hundredth** — written 0.01, because it takes two places after the point. A 10×10 grid shows it: 100 tiny cells fill one whole, so each cell is one hundredth.
Hundredths cut each tenth into ten again.

widget.successFeedback: Between 0.3 and 0.4, six hundredths past the 0.3 mark. 0.36 is not 'thirty-six', it is 3 tenths and 6 hundredths — and the line shows you exactly where that is.
widget.lowFeedback: Your marker is below 0.36. It sits between 0.3 and 0.4.
widget.highFeedback: Your marker is above 0.36. It sits between 0.3 and 0.4, not past it.

predict.prompt: Before you place it: is 0.36 closer to 0 or to 1?
predict.reveal: 0.36 sits 0.36 from 0 and 0.64 from 1 — the 0 side wins. Judging position from the endpoints first makes the exact placement easier to defend.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents smaller rungs.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for smaller rungs must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines smaller rungs.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

explanationVariants: One tenth is a full row of 10 cells on the grid — 10 hundredths.

widget.prompt: How many hundredths make one tenth?

commonErrors.feedback: 100 hundredths make a whole, not a tenth. One tenth is just one row of the grid: 10 hundredths.
1 hundredth is a single cell. A whole tenth is a full row: 10 hundredths.

widget.fallbackFeedback: One tenth is a full row of the 10×10 grid — count the cells in a row.

steps.body: One more rung: split a hundredth into 10 and you get a **thousandth** — written 0.001, three places after the point. The ladder never runs out downward, but Grade 5 stops here: tenths, hundredths, thousandths.

explanationVariants: The third digit after the point is the thousandths place — here, 5.
Counting places past the point: tenths, hundredths, thousandths lands on 5.

widget.prompt: In the number 0.375, which digit is in the THOUSANDTHS place?

options.label: 5 — the third place after the point
options.feedback: Counting past the point — tenths (3), hundredths (7), thousandths (5) — the thousandths digit is 5.

options.label: 3 — it comes first
options.feedback: 3 is the first place after the point, which is TENTHS. The third place, thousandths, is 5.

options.label: 7 — it's in the middle
options.feedback: 7 is the second place, HUNDREDTHS. The third place, thousandths, is 5.

options.label: 0 — the leading zero
options.feedback: The 0 is the ones place, before the point. The thousandths place is the third digit after it: 5.

steps.body: Match each fraction to its decimal.

widget.prompt: Match each fraction to its decimal form.

pairErrors.feedback: 0.7 is 7 TENTHS (7/10). 7/100 is seven hundredths — two places — which is 0.07.

widget.missFeedback: Count the zeros in the denominator: that's how many decimal places the fraction needs.

explanationVariants: Splitting one hundredth into 10 gives 10 thousandths.
Each rung down is a ×10 split, so one hundredth is 10 thousandths.

widget.prompt: How many thousandths make one hundredth?

commonErrors.feedback: 100 thousandths make a tenth, not a hundredth. Each single rung down is a split into 10: one hundredth is 10 thousandths.
1000 thousandths make a whole. Just one hundredth is 10 thousandths.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Every rung down splits one part into 10 — so one hundredth becomes 10 thousandths.

hints: A penny is one hundredth of a dollar — 0.01 of a dollar.
Write 23 hundredths as a decimal of a dollar.
explanationVariants: Each penny is 1/100 of a dollar, so 23 pennies is 23/100 = 0.23.
23 hundredths of a dollar is written 0.23.

widget.prompt: A penny is one hundredth of a dollar. Written as a decimal of a dollar (0.??), how much is 23 pennies? Enter the two-digit hundredths value (the ?? part).

commonErrors.feedback: 230 reads the pennies as thousandths. 23 pennies is 23 hundredths: 0.23.
2 catches only part of the value. 23 pennies is a full 23 hundredths: 0.23.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Each penny is 0.01; 23 of them is 23 hundredths.

takeaways: A hundredth is one of 100 equal parts (0.01, two places); a thousandth is one of 1000 (0.001, three places).
Each rung down splits the one above into 10: 10 hundredths make a tenth, 10 thousandths make a hundredth.
The zeros in a fraction's denominator match the number of decimal places.
steps.teaser: next: the ×10 and ÷10 moves that slide a digit along the whole ladder.

concept.body: Quick rewind. **Each place after the point is ten times smaller than the one before: tenths, then hundredths, then thousandths.** So 0.4 is four tenths, 0.04 is four hundredths, and 0.004 is four thousandths — each zero pushes the 4 one rung smaller.

explanationVariants: 0.04 has the 4 in the second place — hundredths.
Two places after the point is the hundredths place.

widget.prompt: In 0.04, the digit 4 is in which place?

options.label: Hundredths
options.feedback: The second place after the point is hundredths — 0.04 is four hundredths.

options.label: Tenths
options.feedback: Tenths is the FIRST place. Here the tenths digit is 0, and the 4 sits in the second place: hundredths.

options.label: Thousandths
options.feedback: Thousandths is the THIRD place. The 4 is in the second place: hundredths.
